layers.label: Neutron-star crust
layers.explanation: A solid lattice of iron-peaked atomic nuclei, barely a kilometer thick — the 'skin' of an object 20 km across.

layers.label: Neutron superfluid core
layers.explanation: Beneath the crust, free neutrons flow with almost no viscosity — a quantum liquid at the center.

layers.label: Pulsar beams
layers.explanation: Radio beams launched from the magnetic poles, sweeping the sky like lighthouse light as the star rotates.

hotspots.label: Crust — iron lattice
hotspots.description: A thin crystalline crust of iron-rich atomic nuclei — the surface of a city-sized ball with twice the Sun's mass.

hotspots.label: Neutron superfluid core
hotspots.description: Beneath the crust: a sea of free neutrons supporting the star by degeneracy pressure.

hotspots.label: Pulsar beams
hotspots.description: Radio light beamed out the magnetic poles; with each rotation the beam crosses Earth — the ticking pulsar.

hotspots.label: Supernova debris cloud
hotspots.description: The exploded star's envelope expanding around the new remnant, glowing pink and purple as it cools.

hotspots.label: City scale — a 20 km ball
hotspots.description: An outline of a small city floating beside the star to make its size sink in — the whole star sits inside it.

visualStyleNotes: Small glowing blue-white sphere (radius ~0.9) beside a faint wireframe city dome for scale, matched Anatomy Atelier look: clean, warm, uncluttered. Two translucent pale beams sweep from the poles rotating slowly. Surrounding pink-purple translucent cloud like a faint shell, low opacity so it never obscures. Cross-section reveals the crust ring and interior shimmer.
materialNotes: Star body: emissive white-blue core with subtle fresnel rim. Beams: additive blended cones, low opacity. Debris shell: translucent pink-violet, double-sided. City dome: faint dashed white lines to mark radial scale.
assetBrief: Procedural Three.js scene: star sphere with two rotating cone beams, faint debris cloud shell, optional city-size wireframe dome for scale. Cross-section plane works on the star only. Camera at ~4.8 units, auto-rotate on. Hotspot beads ~0.16 radius, consistent with other star scenes.
